scope: Compra DiDi comunicada por el propietario tras pagar con Google Wallet. Desarrollo basado en un aviso real revisado; pruebas y pantallas públicas con valores ficticios.

parser.automationRequires: Explicit reviewed/reconciled own observation preserving interpreted financial fields, verified unambiguous bank alias, notification-date acceptance and explicit enable

inspection.limitation: Only the queried captured events were checked; absence of a bank notice does not prove the bank never emits one. Delivery success is separate from financial review.

unitAndIntegration.database: Disposable local PostgreSQL 16, afp_test_didi_wallet; all 29 existing migrations applied
covers: Exact Wallet DiDi grammar, cents, malformed amounts, midnight in Mexico and delayed delivery
Missing, conflicting, invalid and future fields, foreign currencies and special movements
Bank digital/physical alias resolution, cross-kind ambiguity, unverified/unknown identities and NFC token separation
No date-policy acceptance means review, even with a forced automatic mode
Original unknown receipt remains immutable on replay; explicit reinterpretation is idempotent and creates no expense
Manual review, registration, explicit point reconciliation and activation scoped to one owner/card/parser/date policy
Eight concurrent native API deliveries plus lost-response retry create one expense and receipt
Second device, equal legitimate purchases, manual duplicates and notification revisions retain explicit resolution
Linking preserves personal notes, category, concept and cash contributions
Cross-owner, cross-bank, other-card, unsupported-source and authentication boundaries
Deletion tombstone prevents replay or late notification from silently recreating an expense
Personal corrections, previous analyses and data survive return to observation

mobileBrowser.environment: Local isolated Next.js production build; real UI and HTTP capture APIs, fake Supabase Auth, disposable PostgreSQL; no production environment files
mobileBrowser.developmentRunIssue: One transient GET movements 500 with Unexpected end of JSON input was observed in the development server. The full flow was repeated with a fresh local database and isolated production build; the failure did not recur. No production service was involved.
